summary: Upgrade the SpendCube Streamlit dashboard suite with two major enhancements: (1) PowerBI-style within-page cross-filtering using Streamlit 1.33+ on_select events on Plotly charts, and (2) new analytical chart types aligned to the procurement dashboard blueprint in docs/procurement_spend_cube_v1_dashboard_blueprint.md. The four core analytics pages (Spend Overview, Category Deep Dive, Supplier Deep Dive, Payment Terms) each receive new charts and cross-filter capability. No new backend data is required — all charts work from the existing transactions.parquet (50 columns, 5210 rows). Unit price and quantity fields do not exist in v1 data, so price-per-unit analytics are explicitly out of scope; spend dispersion is used as the proxy for price variation.

decisions.cross_filter_implementation: Use st.plotly_chart(fig, on_select='rerun', key='unique_key') native Streamlit API (available in Streamlit 1.33+, confirmed in installed 1.56). Each page manages its own cross-filter state from the returned event object. No external package needed. Cross-filter is within-page only — no cross-page state sharing in this sprint.
decisions.no_unit_price_data: transactions.parquet has no unit_price, quantity, or uom columns. Blueprint charts requiring unit price (price-volume scatter, best-price extrapolation) are out of scope. Transaction-level base_amount distributions are used as the proxy for spend variation.
decisions.dumbbell_chart_metric: Dumbbell chart on Supplier Deep Dive shows each supplier's avg payment_terms_days vs their category-level median payment_terms_days. This is the most defensible V1 dumbbell given available data — shows which suppliers are on better/worse terms than category peers.
decisions.opportunity_scatter: Opportunity prioritisation scatter on Spend Overview: x=total spend, y=unique supplier count, bubble_size=transaction count, color=category_l1. High spend + many suppliers = fragmentation opportunity. All values computed from transactions.parquet groupby.
decisions.cross_filter_pattern: Each page that has cross-filtering follows this exact pattern: (1) render master chart with on_select='rerun' and a unique key, (2) read points = (event or {}).get('selection', {}).get('points', []) from the returned value, (3) extract labels from point dicts using the relevant key (point['y'] for horizontal bars, point.get('text') for scatter), (4) display a st.caption indicator when cross-filter is active, (5) apply the filter to a derived DataFrame used for all secondary charts only. Click on empty chart area clears the selection automatically (Plotly deselects all).
decisions.page_scope: Only the 4 analytics pages are modified: 01_spend_overview.py, 02_category_deep_dive.py, 03_supplier_deep_dive.py, 04_payment_terms.py. Pages 05-07 (data quality, recommendations, review workstation) are unchanged.

existing_tables.transactions_parquet: data/output/transactions.parquet — 5210 rows, 50 columns. Key fields: base_amount, category_l1, category_l2, canonical_supplier_name, canonical_supplier_id, business_unit, plant_site, payment_terms_days, invoice_month, po_number, is_tail_spend. No unit_price or quantity fields.

patterns_to_follow: All chart functions in dashboard/components/charts.py return go.Figure and never call st.plotly_chart. Rendering happens in page files only.

Streamlit on_select pattern: event = st.plotly_chart(fig, on_select='rerun', key='unique_str', use_container_width=True). Extract points: points = (event or {}).get('selection', {}).get('points', []). For horizontal bar (y is categorical): values = [p['y'] for p in points if 'y' in p]. For scatter with text=: values = [p.get('text') for p in points if p.get('text')]. Show indicator: if values: st.caption(f'Cross-filter active: {", ".join(str(v) for v in values[:3])} — click chart background to clear').
render_filters() from dashboard.components.filters is always called first and returns the globally-filtered DataFrame. Cross-filter is a secondary in-page filter applied to that result.
Absolute imports: pages import from dashboard.app (load_cube_data) and dashboard.components.charts/filters.
Style consistency: all charts use paper_bgcolor=white, plot_bgcolor=white, font=dict(size=12) — apply _LAYOUT from charts.py or replicate inline.

userStories.title: Add boxplot, scatter_bubble, and dumbbell chart helpers to charts.py
userStories.description: Extend dashboard/components/charts.py with three new chart helper functions needed by the upgraded pages. These functions follow the existing pattern: accept a DataFrame and named column args, return a go.Figure, never call st.plotly_chart internally. The existing _LAYOUT dict (paper_bgcolor=white, plot_bgcolor=white, font size 12, yaxis showgrid=False) should be applied to all new charts.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/components/charts.py — add function boxplot(df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str, title: str) -> go.Figure. For each unique value in df[x], add a go.Box trace with y=df.loc[df[x]==val, y], name=val, boxpoints='outliers'. Apply paper_bgcolor=white, plot_bgcolor=white, font size 12, yaxis showgrid=False, showlegend=False, title=title. Return the figure.

Edit file: dashboard/components/charts.py — add function scatter_bubble(df: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str, size: str, color: str, label: str, title: str, hover_name: str = None) -> go.Figure. Use px.scatter(df, x=x, y=y, size=size, color=color, text=label, title=title, hover_name=hover_name or label, size_max=60). Apply paper_bgcolor=white, font size 12. Call fig.update_traces(textposition='top center') and fig.update_traces(selector=dict(mode='markers+text'), textfont_size=9). Return the figure.

Edit file: dashboard/components/charts.py — add function dumbbell(df: pd.DataFrame, label_col: str, left_col: str, right_col: str, left_name: str, right_name: str, title: str) -> go.Figure. Implementation: create a go.Figure. For each row in df.itertuples(), add a go.Scatter trace with x=[row.left_col_val, row.right_col_val], y=[row.label_col_val, row.label_col_val], mode='lines', line=dict(color='#bdc3c7', width=1.5), showlegend=False. After all lines, add two go.Scatter traces for all dots: left dots (x=df[left_col], y=df[label_col], mode='markers', marker=dict(color='#e74c3c', size=10), name=left_name) and right dots (x=df[right_col], y=df[label_col], mode='markers', marker=dict(color='#2980b9', size=10), name=right_name). Apply paper_bgcolor=white, plot_bgcolor=white, font size 12, yaxis=dict(showgrid=False, autorange='reversed'), xaxis=dict(showgrid=True, gridcolor='#f0f0f0'), title=title. Return the figure.

Run: PYTHONPATH=$(pwd) python3 -c "from dashboard.components.charts import boxplot, scatter_bubble, dumbbell; import pandas as pd; df = pd.DataFrame({'a':['x','y','x'], 'b':[1,2,3]}); f=boxplot(df,'a','b','t'); print('boxplot OK'); df2=pd.DataFrame({'x':[1,2],'y':[1,2],'s':[10,20],'c':['A','B'],'l':['p','q']}); f2=scatter_bubble(df2,'x','y','s','c','l','t'); print('scatter OK'); df3=pd.DataFrame({'lbl':['A','B'],'left':[10,20],'right':[30,40]}); f3=dumbbell(df3,'lbl','left','right','L','R','t'); print('dumbbell OK')" — should print all three OK lines

userStories.title: Upgrade Supplier Deep Dive with payment terms dumbbell and cross-filtering
userStories.description: Enhance dashboard/pages/03_supplier_deep_dive.py with a payment terms dumbbell chart and cross-filtering. The dumbbell shows for the selected supplier's top 15 transaction groups (by category or all transactions): for each of the top 15 suppliers by spend within the current filtered view, show their avg payment_terms_days (red, left) vs the median payment_terms_days for their primary category across ALL transactions (blue, right). Cross-filtering: clicking a category in the spend-by-category chart filters the monthly trend to that category. Note: the dumbbell is supplier-level; it shows all selected supplier's data vs category benchmark.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/03_supplier_deep_dive.py — add import: from dashboard.components.charts import horizontal_bar, dumbbell (update existing import line to include dumbbell).

Edit file: dashboard/pages/03_supplier_deep_dive.py — add function _payment_terms_dumbbell(sup_df: pd.DataFrame, all_txn: pd.DataFrame) -> None. Logic: (1) if sup_df.empty or 'payment_terms_days' not in sup_df.columns: st.info('No payment terms data.'); return. (2) Filter sup_df: has_terms = sup_df[sup_df['payment_terms_days'].notna()]. If has_terms.empty: st.info('No payment terms recorded for this supplier.'); return. (3) Compute supplier avg terms: sup_avg = float(has_terms['payment_terms_days'].mean()). (4) Determine primary category: primary_cat = has_terms['category_l1'].mode().iloc[0] if 'category_l1' in has_terms.columns and not has_terms['category_l1'].dropna().empty else None. (5) Compute category median from all_txn: if primary_cat and 'payment_terms_days' in all_txn.columns: cat_median = float(all_txn[all_txn['category_l1']==primary_cat]['payment_terms_days'].dropna().median()) else: cat_median = float(all_txn['payment_terms_days'].dropna().median()) if 'payment_terms_days' in all_txn.columns else None. (6) If cat_median is None: st.info('Category benchmark unavailable.'); return. (7) Build single-row df: row_df = pd.DataFrame({'Supplier': [sup_df['canonical_supplier_name'].iloc[0] if 'canonical_supplier_name' in sup_df.columns else 'Selected Supplier'], 'Avg Terms (days)': [sup_avg], 'Category Median (days)': [cat_median]}). (8) Call: fig = dumbbell(row_df, label_col='Supplier', left_col='Avg Terms (days)', right_col='Category Median (days)', left_name='Supplier Avg', right_name='Category Median', title=f'Payment Terms vs Category Median ({primary_cat or "All Categories"})'). (9) Render: st.plotly_chart(fig, use_container_width=True). (10) Add caption: supplier_below = sup_avg < cat_median; msg = f'This supplier is on {"shorter" if supplier_below else "longer"} terms ({sup_avg:.0f}d) than the {primary_cat or "overall"} category median ({cat_median:.0f}d). {"Working capital opportunity: negotiate extension." if supplier_below else "Terms are favourable."}'; st.caption(msg).

risks: Streamlit on_select returns point data in different shapes depending on chart type. For horizontal bar charts, point['y'] gives the category label. For scatter charts, point.get('text') gives the text= value (supplier name). If the actual event structure differs at runtime, Ralph must inspect the live event dict and adjust the key extraction accordingly.

The dumbbell chart is a single-row dumbbell when viewing one selected supplier — this is intentional. If Ralph finds the single-row dumbbell too sparse, it should expand to show the top N suppliers in the filtered view each with their own dumbbell row (same function, build agg per supplier).

scatter_bubble with text= labels may be cluttered when 50+ suppliers are shown. The acceptance criteria include textfont_size=9 and top-center position, but Ralph may also filter to top 30 by spend for label display while keeping all bubbles.
